blocks.text: Origin / creation. Opponents of Reduction organized around preserving complete DBA persons, language, archives, worlds, and institutions.
Identity / human status. Artificial philosophical and political coalition.
Importance. They exposed the moral cost of choosing simplification for future beings who could not consent and prevented Reduction from becoming an unquestioned technical program.

Decline or loss. Infrastructure could no longer support their preferred future. Some refused reduction and died or entered dormancy; others negotiated stronger consent, archive, and identity safeguards before accepting the Resolution.

Final status / surviving function. No confirmed active coalition remains. Their objections survive in sleeping archives, the right to refuse, and Era Four debates over restoration and historical loss.
